companies.name: Start the shop
companies.plain_english: Java calls this method to start the Shopizer application. It hands startup over to Spring Boot.
companies.sequence_reason: First, find the real application's entry point. This is where Java hands control to Spring Boot; every later company makes more sense once you see how Shopizer starts.

interview.question: What happens after Java calls ShopApplication.main(), and how does SpringApplication.run() start a Spring Boot application?

companies.name: Check that the shop has started
companies.plain_english: When Spring Boot says the shop is ready, this method finds the current working folder and writes it to the application log.

inbound.name: Spring Boot ready event
inbound.description: Spring invokes this method for ApplicationReadyEvent; Company 1 does not call it directly.

outbound.name: Read working folder
outbound.description: System.getProperty("user.dir") reads the current working directory.

outbound.name: Write startup log
outbound.description: logger.info writes a message containing the working directory.

companies.sequence_reason: Second, observe startup completion before exploring individual web features. This method shows how the app logs its working directory when Spring announces readiness. Learning order only: Spring's ApplicationReadyEvent actually fires after startup configuration, not before Companies 3–6.

interview.question: How does @EventListener(ApplicationReadyEvent.class) differ from @PostConstruct, and why might it be too late for essential startup configuration?

companies.name: Set up request filtering
companies.type: Spring Boot bean for XSS servlet filter registration
companies.plain_english: Registers a request filter for the shop, API, and customer URLs. It creates an XssFilter and tells Spring Boot which web requests should pass through it.

inbound.name: Spring creates the filter bean
inbound.description: The @Bean annotation lets Spring call this method while configuring the application.

outbound.name: Build filter registration
outbound.description: Creates a FilterRegistrationBean to connect the filter to web requests.

outbound.name: Shopizer XssFilter
outbound.description: Creates a real Shopizer XssFilter; its implementation has not been assigned a company number yet.

companies.sequence_reason: Third, introduce incoming-request protection before teaching responses and routes. This factory method registers a Shopizer XssFilter for shop, API and customer URL patterns.

interview.question: How does FilterRegistrationBean control which URLs a servlet filter applies to, and why is an XSS filter not a replacement for output encoding?

companies.name: Prepare JSON responses
companies.plain_english: Adds Jackson's JSON converter so Spring MVC can read and write JSON in web requests and responses.

inbound.name: Spring MVC configuration
inbound.description: Spring MVC calls this WebMvcConfigurer override while setting up message converters.

outbound.name: Create Jackson JSON converter
outbound.description: Adds a MappingJackson2HttpMessageConverter to the converter list.

companies.sequence_reason: Fourth, learn how data travels between clients and the Java backend after seeing basic request filtering. This method shows the JSON conversion mechanism before you study routes and controller behavior.

interview.question: What happens to Spring MVC's default HttpMessageConverters when you override configureMessageConverters(), and when should you use extendMessageConverters() instead?

companies.name: Set up the shop homepage
companies.plain_english: Maps a visit to the website's root address (/) to a view named shop, without requiring a separate controller method.

inbound.name: Spring MVC configuration
inbound.description: Spring MVC calls this WebMvcConfigurer hook to register simple view routes.

companies.sequence_reason: Fifth, after learning how HTTP data is handled, see how the application attaches a URL to a page. The single root mapping makes routing concrete before introducing request interceptors.

interview.question: When would you use ViewControllerRegistry.addViewController() instead of writing a @Controller method, and what does setViewName("shop") actually resolve?

companies.name: Add request interceptors
companies.plain_english: Adds a locale-change interceptor and a CORS interceptor; the active CORS registration targets /services/** and /api/**.

inbound.name: Spring MVC configuration
inbound.description: Spring MVC invokes this WebMvcConfigurer override to install request interceptors.

outbound.name: Company 8 — Create language-change interceptor
outbound.description: Calls localeChangeInterceptor() at line 80; opens Company 8.

outbound.name: Company 9 — Create CORS interceptor
outbound.description: Calls corsFilter() at line 92; opens Company 9.

outbound.name: Set interceptor URL patterns
outbound.description: Adds /services/** and /api/** to the active CORS interceptor registration (lines 94–96).

companies.sequence_reason: Sixth, after establishing the homepage route, introduce cross-cutting work performed around MVC requests. This method registers locale and CORS interceptors. Its commented-out storeFilter block is not active code.

interview.question: How is a Spring MVC HandlerInterceptor different from a servlet Filter, and what happens when you register one without addPathPatterns()?

companies.type: Spring MVC and Spring Boot web configuration
companies.name: Handle images and binary downloads
companies.plain_english: Creates a byte-array HTTP converter that supports JPEG, GIF, PNG, and general binary downloads.

inbound.name: Spring creates the binary converter
inbound.description: Spring calls this @Bean method to create a converter during configuration.

outbound.name: List accepted media types
outbound.description: Uses Arrays.asList with IMAGE_JPEG, IMAGE_GIF, IMAGE_PNG, APPLICATION_OCTET_STREAM.

outbound.name: Build byte-array converter
outbound.description: Constructs ByteArrayHttpMessageConverter and sets its supported media types at line 106.

companies.sequence_reason: Seventh, extend Company 4's HTTP response lesson beyond JSON: images and downloaded files use bytes and media types instead of structured JSON. The source places this factory after MVC interceptor registration; numbering is for learning, not runtime execution.

interview.question: When would you return byte[] through ByteArrayHttpMessageConverter instead of a Jackson JSON converter, and how do supported media types affect content negotiation?

companies.type: Spring MVC and Spring Boot web configuration
companies.name: Create the language-change interceptor
companies.plain_english: Creates the interceptor that can change a visitor's language using the request's locale parameter.

inbound.name: Company 6 — Register request interceptors
inbound.description: Company 6 calls localeChangeInterceptor() inside addInterceptors() at line 80.

inbound.name: Spring creates the interceptor bean
inbound.description: Spring can also obtain this instance through the @Bean factory method.

companies.sequence_reason: Eighth, open the concrete factory behind Company 6's localeChangeInterceptor() call. You have already seen where this interceptor is registered; now you can inspect where its actual object is created.

interview.question: How does LocaleChangeInterceptor work together with a LocaleResolver, and why does changing a locale parameter require an appropriate resolver?

companies.type: Spring MVC and Spring Boot web configuration
companies.name: Create the CORS interceptor
companies.plain_english: Creates Shopizer's CorsFilter object, which Company 6 registers for service and API request paths.

inbound.name: Company 6 — Register request interceptors
inbound.description: Company 6 invokes corsFilter() at line 92 to add the object as an MVC interceptor.

inbound.name: Spring creates the CORS bean
inbound.description: The @Bean method makes this Shopizer object available as a Spring bean.

outbound.name: Build Shopizer CorsFilter
outbound.description: Creates a real com.salesmanager.shop.filter.CorsFilter instance; the class implementation is not yet separately mapped.

companies.sequence_reason: Ninth, inspect the second real factory called by Company 6. After the language interceptor, this method supplies the CORS component used for API and service paths. Although named CorsFilter, it is passed to Spring's addInterceptor() in Company 6.

interview.question: Shopizer names this bean corsFilter() but registers it through InterceptorRegistry.addInterceptor(). What must its Java type support, and how would you verify whether it is an MVC interceptor rather than a servlet Filter?

companies.type: Spring MVC and Spring Boot web configuration
companies.name: Choose the default language
companies.plain_english: Creates a session-based language resolver and sets its starting language to the server's default locale.

inbound.name: Spring creates the locale resolver
inbound.description: The @Bean method provides a SessionLocaleResolver for Spring MVC.

outbound.name: Read default JVM locale
outbound.description: Sets its default locale to Locale.getDefault().

companies.sequence_reason: Tenth, return to Company 8's language feature and learn where Spring stores and resolves a visitor's locale. The interceptor can request changes; the SessionLocaleResolver provides the locale-resolution mechanism.

interview.question: Why would you choose SessionLocaleResolver instead of AcceptHeaderLocaleResolver in Spring MVC, and what happens when the browser session is lost?

companies.type: Spring MVC and Spring Boot web configuration
companies.name: Load translated messages
companies.plain_english: Creates a UTF-8 message source using Shopizer's shopizer, messages, shipping, and payment resource bundles.

inbound.name: Spring creates the message source
inbound.description: Spring registers the returned ReloadableResourceBundleMessageSource as a bean.

outbound.name: Select four translation bundles
outbound.description: Adds classpath bundle basenames for shopizer, messages, shipping, and payment at lines 136–140.

companies.sequence_reason: Eleventh, finish the locale flow: Company 8 responds to a language request, Company 10 resolves the active locale, and this company supplies translated text from the application's message bundles.

interview.question: How does ReloadableResourceBundleMessageSource choose a locale-specific properties file, and why should you define both basenames and UTF-8 encoding?

numbering_policy: IDs are permanent. Assign dotted subsidiary numbers only to verified parent/child methods; event-driven steps and external APIs are links, not automatic subsidiaries.
sequence_policy: Company numbers indicate a developer's learning path, NOT execution order. Java/Spring runtime lifecycle can differ: the readiness event occurs after startup configuration. Keep parent/subsidiary IDs based on genuine nesting/dependency evidence.
education_policy: Every company requires a unique stable interview.id, interview.question and a plain-English sequence_reason grounded in actual source. No duplicate questions.
